The semantic masking mechanism proposed in this study is designed and implemented based on the DQN architecture. To verify the incremental value of this mechanism, a multi-dimensional comparison between the original DQN and the DQN with semantic masking is required. To ensure the fairness of experimental comparison and the reproducibility of results, both types of DQN models are trained with the same random seed, and all hyperparameters are kept completely consistent. To further validate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed framework, Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA) and Differential Evolution (DE) are additionally introduced as baseline models in this study. The PSO algorithm is implemented directly using the pyswarm library. Except for the hyperparameters requiring adjustment, all other parameters utilize the library's default configuration. The hyperparameters of all baseline algorithms are tuned and determined according to the convergence characteristics and variation amplitude of the optimal value of the objective function observed in real time. The results are shown in the Table 5. DQN takes maximizing the reward function as its optimization objective, while PSO, WOA, and DE all aim to minimize the objective function to obtain the globally optimal combination of energy storage actions. To ensure the consistency of optimization objectives among different algorithms and the rationality of comparison, this study uses the negative value of the DQN reward function as the objective function of these three algorithms, thus unifying the optimization direction of all comparative models.

In the performance evaluation of all models, the total system operating cost
( \mathrm { O p e } _ { \mathrm { c o s t } } )
and total grid electricity consumption
( \mathrm { T o t a l } _ { \mathrm { G r i d } } )
serve as core focus metrics. These two factors directly correlate with the economic viability (operating costs) and environmental impact (grid dependency) of the microgrid during the experimental operation period. Secondly, the study aims to achieve cost reduction and grid electricity purchase reduction through the charging and discharging scheduling of energy storage systems, while ensuring that the energy difference between the initial and final states of energy storage approaches zero (energy storage state closed-loop). Therefore, the SOC status (Bat
diff
) (SOC at the end of the experimental period, the average and standard deviation SOC at 23:00 every day) is also an important comparative indicator for the energy storage system. To reduce the generation of useless actions during training and decrease the frequency of action clipping caused by violating physical constraints, the boundary trigger count of the energy storage system
\mathrm { ( B a t _ { b o u n d a r y } ) }
(action exceeds the remaining chargeable or dischargeable capacity of the energy storage system/ discharging action exceeds the remaining load.) is incorporated into the evaluation system to reflect the operational safety of the strategy and the effectiveness of actions. Finally, considering the core operational requirement of discharging during peak electricity rates and charging during valley periods in microgrids, the amount of electricity purchased from the grid during peak pricing periods
( \mathrm { G r i d } _ { \mathrm { p e a k } } )
serves as a key metric for evaluating the peak shaving effectiveness of strategies.
To further verify the optimization effect of semantic masking on the training process of traditional DQN, the study adds two supplementary evaluation dimensions from the perspective of training dynamic characteristics. The reward value in the initial training phase
( \mathrm { R } _ { \mathrm { I n i t i a l } } )
is used to evaluate the initial learning efficiency of the strategy. The standard deviation of rewards in the last 100 training rounds
( \mathrm { R } _ { \mathrm { S t a n d a r d } } )
is used to quantify the stability of the strategy in the late training stage. For the performance comparison between the group search algorithm and DQN, the evaluation dimensions

4. Results
4.1 EV Electricity Consumption Data Generation Results
Based on real data and the real-time charging behavior generation mechanism of charging piles, this study constructs an energy consumption dataset for 50 charging piles across 10 regions. By comparing the generation results of four methods with real data, the model with the smallest RMSE was selected as the optimal generation scheme.
